videos.subject: Walking gives you more ideas
videos.script: You get about sixty percent more ideas just by walking. Researchers had people brainstorm sitting down, then on a treadmill. Same room. Same blank wall. Walking, their ideas jumped. And it lasted after they sat back down. So when you're stuck, don't stare at the problem. Get up and walk. Because

videos.script: The same dress sold more at thirty-nine dollars than at thirty-four. A clothing catalog printed different prices for different customers. Thirty-four. Thirty-nine. Forty-four. videos.subject: You'd miss a gorilla in plain sight
videos.script: Almost half the people watching missed a gorilla walking right through the video. Their task: count the passes in a basketball video. Halfway through, a gorilla walks in, thumps its chest, and walks off. Afterwards they asked: what gorilla? When your brain focuses, it hides everything else. So next time you're sure nothing happened, remember:
videos.hook_text: Count the passes. Miss the gorilla.

videos.subject: Why coins disappear faster than bills
videos.script: You spend more when your money comes in small change. Students got one dollar, to keep or spend on candy. Four quarters? Sixty-three percent spent it. One bill? Only twenty-six percent. Same dollar. Your brain guards a big note, and lets small change go. So to save more, carry bigger notes. Because

videos.subject: Money keeps buying happiness, for most
videos.script: More money keeps making most people happier, way past seventy-five thousand. Even the scientist behind that famous limit helped test it. Thirty-three thousand workers rated their mood on their phones. Happiness kept rising, up to half a million a year. Only the unhappiest fifth levelled off, around a hundred thousand.
